result:
I made both changes T-DG7-DO-K1 asked for. All the required acceptance checks exit 0. The extra run of the release-tooling tests (`tools/release/tests`) exits 1, with 4 failures; none of them comes from these edits. I ran from 21:36 to 22:15 UTC, about 39 minutes. Nothing is committed.

**1. Proxy note in `e2e/support/keycloak-login.ts`.** Only the header comment changed. The run command now starts with `env -u` to unset `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and their lower-case forms. A new paragraph says the alternative is to put the identity provider's host name in `NO_PROXY`. It also records:
- the evidence: host run 3b had 4 tests fail on the 60 s timeout; run 3c, the same command without the proxy variables, passed 4 of 4;
- that the cause is inferred, not verified, and is a property of the test host only; no product code, Compose file or TLS rule changes;
- that a host whose proxy settings can't be changed records this test as BLOCKED, never as a pass.

I could not run the Keycloak test itself here because there is no Docker daemon, so it is BLOCKED in this environment.

**2. `automation_rule` known-limitations row.** The tool `tools/release/known-limitations.mjs` only generates sections 1–3, and this row is an architecture-decision residual. Its home is the hand-written section 6 of `docs/handover/known-limitations.md`, and that file and its Arabic summary belong to the devops role. So I added the row directly: BE-F2's proposed text plus the ADR-0065 point that a target installation recreates its rules by hand. I also added a provisional Arabic line to `known-limitations.ar-summary.md`, then regenerated.

**Checks:**

| Check | Exit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DG6 historical validator, before and after | 0 | PASS |
| `known-limitations.mjs --check` before regenerating | 1 | Already failing at HEAD: DO-J's `release-notes.md` now contains Arabic and wasn't listed. Regenerating added that one line |
| `known-limitations.mjs --check` after `--write` | 0 | PASS |
| `check-handover.mjs` | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm test` | 0 | 3022 + 2179 + 259 tests pass |
| Contract test on a disposable PostgreSQL | 0 | 111 of 111 |
| Prettier over all files | 0 | PASS |
| Release-tooling tests (`node --test tools/release/tests/*.test.mjs …`) | 1 | 458 pass, 4 fail |

The 4 failures:
- **T-A5:** the sandbox makes the pnpm store read-only, so the build-from-archive install fails. Environment limit, BLOCKED here.
- **Two `check-handover.test.mjs` cases:** their test setup copies the real `docs/handover`, which now contains `release-notes.md` and `guides/`. They expect BLOCKED and get PASS; this was already the case before my edits.
- **T-M2:** I wrote log files into the repo while it ran. Run on its own it passes 10 of 10.

**Open points:**
- Section 4 of `known-limitations.md` still says the live Keycloak sign-in "has never run in the delivery environment", and the `keycloak-e2e` dependency is still `blocked`. D-267 records the 4/4 pass in host run 3c. Fixing the status needs a change to `environment.md`, which isn't a devops file, and your decision on how the host run counts. I left both unchanged.
- Should the two `check-handover.test.mjs` cases be routed for repair before the freeze?

The handback is `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-K1-devops-engineer.md`, with logs and checksums in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-K1-evidence/`.
